confidence_notes: I ran four web searches: the RBA rate, general Bilbao prices, a Numbeo-based check, and Bilbao cocktail and wine prices. Restaurant meals, beer and coffee rest on aggregated cost-of-living data. A Numbeo snapshot republished by Expatica (June 2026) gives about EUR 18.74 for an inexpensive meal, EUR 65.07 for a three-course meal for two, and EUR 3.38 for a 0.5 L domestic draught beer. MyLifeElsewhere gives lower figures, roughly EUR 15 for a meal with a drink and EUR 3.24 for a pint. Cappuccino sources conflict slightly, at EUR 2.04 to 2.12, so I used about EUR 2.3 for central and tourist areas. Cocktail and wine data are thin. The cocktail figure comes from an Expatistan item of about EUR 10 and travel-guide ranges of EUR 9 to 14 for premium gin and tonic. Wine guides give EUR 2 to 3.50 at pintxos bars, so I set the glass at the upper end for a sit-down restaurant. I did not search for exchange rates other than the RBA's AUD/USD. I converted EUR prices to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.16 USD per EUR, from general knowledge and not verified by search. All four accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Bilbao as a popular, fairly pricey northern Spanish city in peak summer. I did not inspect any listings or booking pages, and accommodation is the least certain group.
comparable_city_reasoning: Bilbao is priced slightly above the Spanish average. Cost-of-living sources put restaurants about 15% above the national average. It is broadly comparable to San Sebastian, though cheaper, and to Valencia or Seville in the mid-range. It is cheaper than Barcelona for accommodation and above typical interior Spanish cities.
